title: 实验 5-14 · PWM + RC 低通 = 最便宜的 DAC
summary: ESP32 的 PWM 引脚经 10 kΩ / 1 µF 低通滤波，得到平均值 = 占空比 × 3.3 V 的直流电压，再用 ADC1 读回来。看看纹波怎样随 PWM 频率和 RC 变化，以及“纹波小”和“响应快”之间的取舍。
description: **目标**：用 PWM 加一级 RC 低通做一个简易 DAC：验证输出平均值 V̄ = D × 3.3 V，并看纹波怎样随占空比、频率和 RC 变化。

**电路**：ESP32 插在 b1，USB 供电。任意一个能输出 PWM 的 GPIO（参考答案用 GPIO27，i11）→ R1 **10 kΩ** → 结点 VDAC；VDAC 接 C1 **1 µF** 到 GND，同时用跳线接到一个 **ADC1** 引脚（参考答案用 GPIO34，i5），让芯片自己把滤波后的电压读回来。GND：j14 → bn14。示波器 CH1 接 VDAC，CH2 接 PWM 引脚（可选，只用来看波形）。
**引脚设置**：ADC 引脚设成“模拟输入 ADC”；PWM 引脚设成“PWM 输出”。测试会自动改占空比（25 / 50 / 75 %）和频率（100 Hz / 1 kHz / 10 kHz）。
**原理**：PWM 是在 0 V 和 3.3 V 之间切换的方波，它的平均值（直流分量）是 D × 3.3 V，其余是 f、2f、3f…… 的交流分量。RC 低通的截止频率 fc = 1/(2πRC)；只要 fc 远低于 PWM 频率，交流分量几乎全被滤掉，只剩直流。
**纹波公式**（τ ≫ T 时，电容电压近似线性地上下爬）：高电平期间电容电流 ≈ (3.3 − V̄)/R，持续 D·T；所以 **ΔV ≈ 3.3 V × D(1 − D) / (f·R·C)**。τ 和 T 差不多时用精确值 3.3 × tanh(T/4τ)（50 % 占空比）。
**先预测**：fc 是多少？25 / 50 / 75 % 时 VDAC 的平均值和 12 位 ADC 读数各是多少？1 kHz 下哪个占空比纹波最大，各是多少 mV？100 Hz 和 10 kHz、50 % 时纹波又是多少？
- VDAC 的**平均值**（示波器 vavg）和 ADC 读数：验证 V̄ = D × 3.3 V，PWM + RC 就是一个 DAC；
- VDAC 的**纹波**（vpp）：滤波没滤干净的那部分，决定了这个 DAC 的“噪声”；
- 不同频率下的纹波：说明为什么要让 τ = RC ≫ PWM 周期 T。电路检查通过后，把读数填进下面的「测量」（以你自己的面包板为准）；答完后会显示计算对比。
**取舍：纹波 vs 建立时间**：RC 越大纹波越小，但输出跟随占空比变化也越慢。占空比突变后，VDAC 按 τ = RC = **10 ms** 指数逼近新值：到 1 % 以内要 4.6τ ≈ 46 ms，到 12 位的 1 LSB 以内要约 8.3τ ≈ 83 ms。所以：
- 想要纹波小又响应快 → **提高 PWM 频率**（纹波 ∝ 1/f，不影响 τ）；
- 还不够 → 用**两级 RC**（二阶，纹波按 (f/fc)² 下降）或有源滤波器。
**实际项目经验**：
- ESP32 的 PWM（LEDC）频率和分辨率是绑在一起的：f × 2^位数 ≤ 80 MHz。10 位分辨率最高约 78 kHz，8 位约 312 kHz；要 12 位只能 ≤ 19.5 kHz。DAC 用途选“够高的频率 + 够用的位数”。
- ESP32 其实有两个真正的 8 位 DAC：**GPIO25、GPIO26**（ESP32-S3 / C3 没有）。只要 8 位、并且引脚空着，直接用它们更省事；需要更多路或更高分辨率时才用 PWM + RC。
- STM32F103C8 没有 DAC（F103RC 以上才有），PWM + RC 是最常见的替代方案。
- ESP32 的 ADC 本身不线性：两端（< 0.1 V、> 3.1 V，11 dB 衰减时）几乎读不准，中间也有 ±几十 LSB 的误差；用 `esp_adc_cal` 校准，或者只做相对比较。这里读到的 1023 / 2045 / 3068 是理想 ADC。
- ADC 读 PWM 滤波电压时要“同步”或多次取平均，否则纹波会混进读数。
**模型说明**：PWM 输出级是理想开关串 25 Ω；ADC 用直流模型（等于 PWM 平均值，看不到纹波）；示波器测量取稳态后的最后两个周期；电容是理想的（没有漏电和 ESR）。

en.title: Experiment 5-14 · PWM + RC low-pass = the cheapest DAC
en.summary: An ESP32 PWM pin through a 10 kΩ / 1 µF low-pass gives a DC voltage equal to duty × 3.3 V, read back by ADC1. See how the ripple depends on the PWM frequency and RC, and the trade-off between low ripple and fast response.
description: **Goal**: build a simple DAC from PWM and one RC low-pass: check that the output average is V̄ = D × 3.3 V, and see how the ripple depends on duty cycle, frequency and RC.

**Circuit**: an ESP32 at b1, powered from USB. Any PWM-capable GPIO (the solution uses GPIO27, i11) → R1 **10 kΩ** → node VDAC; VDAC has C1 **1 µF** to GND and a jumper to an **ADC1** pin (the solution uses GPIO34, i5), so the chip reads the filtered voltage back itself. GND: j14 → bn14. Scope CH1 on VDAC, CH2 on the PWM pin (optional, just to look at the waveforms).
**Pin table settings**: the ADC pin as "analog input (ADC)"; the PWM pin as "PWM output". The tests change the duty cycle (25 / 50 / 75 %) and the frequency (100 Hz / 1 kHz / 10 kHz).

**How it works**: PWM is a square wave switching between 0 V and 3.3 V. Its average (DC component) is D × 3.3 V; the rest is AC at f, 2f, 3f… The RC low-pass cuts off at fc = 1/(2πRC); as long as fc is far below the PWM frequency, almost all of the AC is removed and the DC remains.

**Ripple formula** (for τ ≫ T the capacitor voltage ramps almost linearly up and down): during the high time the capacitor current is ≈ (3.3 − V̄)/R for D·T, so **ΔV ≈ 3.3 V × D(1 − D) / (f·R·C)**. When τ is comparable to T use the exact value 3.3 × tanh(T/4τ) (50 % duty).

**Predict first**: what is fc? What are the VDAC average and the 12-bit ADC reading at 25 / 50 / 75 %? At 1 kHz, which duty cycle gives the largest ripple, and how many mV each? What is the ripple at 100 Hz and at 10 kHz with 50 %?
**Measure**:
- the **average** of VDAC (scope vavg) and the ADC reading: checks V̄ = D × 3.3 V — PWM + RC is a DAC;
- the **ripple** of VDAC (vpp): what the filter didn't remove, the "noise" of this DAC;

- the ripple at different frequencies: why τ = RC must be ≫ the PWM period T. Once the circuit check passes, type your readings into the Measurements below (whatever your own board shows); the worked comparison appears after you answer.

**Trade-off: ripple vs settling time**: a bigger RC means less ripple but a slower response to a duty change. After a step, VDAC approaches the new value with τ = RC = **10 ms**: within 1 % after 4.6τ ≈ 46 ms, within one 12-bit LSB after about 8.3τ ≈ 83 ms. So:
- low ripple *and* fast response → **raise the PWM frequency** (ripple ∝ 1/f, τ unchanged);
- still not enough → **two RC stages** (second order: ripple falls as (f/fc)²) or an active filter.
**Rule of thumb for real projects**:

- ESP32 PWM (LEDC) frequency and resolution are tied: f × 2^bits ≤ 80 MHz. 10-bit resolution tops out around 78 kHz, 8-bit around 312 kHz; 12-bit only up to 19.5 kHz. For a DAC pick "a high enough frequency + enough bits".
- The ESP32 has two real 8-bit DACs on **GPIO25 and GPIO26** (not on the ESP32-S3 / C3). If 8 bits are enough and the pins are free, just use them; PWM + RC is for more channels or more resolution.
- The STM32F103C8 has no DAC (only the F103RC and up do), so PWM + RC is the usual substitute.

- The ESP32 ADC is not linear: near the ends (< 0.1 V, > 3.1 V at 11 dB attenuation) it barely reads, and in the middle it is off by tens of LSB. Calibrate with `esp_adc_cal` or only compare relative values. The 1023 / 2045 / 3068 here are an ideal ADC.
- When the ADC reads a filtered PWM voltage, synchronise or average several samples, or the ripple leaks into the reading.

**Model note**: the PWM output stage is an ideal switch behind 25 Ω; the ADC uses the DC model (the PWM average, so it doesn't see the ripple); scope measurements use the last two periods after steady state; the capacitor is ideal (no leakage, no ESR).
compare: - fc = 1/(2π × 10 kΩ × 1 µF) ≈ **16 Hz**, far below the 1 kHz PWM.
- 1 kHz, 50 %: 3.3 × 0.25 / (1000 × 10 ms) ≈ 82 mV (simulated **82 mV**); 1 kHz, 25 % and 75 %: D(1 − D) = 0.1875, ≈ 62 mV (simulated **62 mV**) — the ripple is largest at 50 %.

- 100 Hz, 50 %: τ is only one period; the approximation gives 0.83 V, the exact value 3.3 × tanh(T/4τ) ≈ 0.81 V (simulated **0.81 Vpp**, VDAC swings between 1.25 V and 2.05 V) — that is no longer "DC".
- 10 kHz, 50 %: ≈ 8 mV (simulated **8.2 mV**), more than one 12-bit ADC LSB (0.8 mV) but already quite flat.

- The ESP32 ADC pin draws no current, so there is no loading error; a 10 kΩ load on VDAC would form a divider with R1 and halve the average — buffer it with an op-amp follower if you need to drive something.

measurements.ask: 1 kHz, 25 %: multimeter DC range on VDAC to GND (the average)
measurements.explain: V̄ = D × 3.3 V ≈ 0.82 V (an ADC reading of about 1023).

measurements.ask: From your reading, the duty cycle D = V̄ / 3.3 V
measurements.explain: ≈ 0.25: the RC low-pass keeps only the PWM's DC component (its average), so PWM + RC is a DAC.

measurements.ask: 1 kHz, 50 %: VDAC's ripple Vpp on the scope
measurements.explain: For τ ≫ T the ripple ≈ 3.3 × D(1 − D) / (f·RC) = 3.3 × 0.25 / (1000 × 10 ms) ≈ 82 mV, largest at 50 %.
τ is only one period, so the approximation breaks down: 3.3 × tanh(T/4τ) ≈ 0.81 V, VDAC swings between about 1.25 V and 2.05 V — no longer DC.
Ripple ∝ 1/f: about 8 mV, a tenth of the 1 kHz value, with the same average. Raising the PWM frequency cuts ripple without slowing the output (τ is unchanged).

hints: PWM pin → 10 kΩ → VDAC; 1 µF from VDAC to GND; a jumper from VDAC to an ADC1 pin (GPIO32–39).
Set the ADC pin to analog input and the other pin to PWM.
The average is duty × 3.3 V; the ripple shrinks with a higher frequency or a bigger RC.
tests: 1 kHz, 50 %: sensible average, the largest ripple
100 Hz, 50 %: τ = T, a big ripple — no longer DC
10 kHz, 50 %: a tiny ripple, the same average

tests.name: 100 Hz、50 %：τ = T，纹波很大，已经不是直流了

compare: - fc = 1/(2π × 10 kΩ × 1 µF) ≈ **16 Hz**，远低于 1 kHz 的 PWM 频率。
- 100 Hz、50 %：τ 只等于一个周期，近似公式给 0.83 V，精确值 3.3 × tanh(T/4τ) ≈ 0.81 V（仿真 **0.81 Vpp**，VDAC 在 1.25 V 和 2.05 V 之间摆）——这已经不是“直流”了。
- 10 kHz、50 %：≈ 8 mV（仿真 **8.2 mV**），比 12 位 ADC 的 1 LSB（0.8 mV）大，但已经很平了。
- ESP32 的 ADC 引脚不取电流，所以没有负载误差；如果 VDAC 后面接一个 10 kΩ 的负载，它和 R1 会组成分压，平均值会掉一半——要接负载就加一个运放跟随器。

measurements.ask: 1 kHz、25 %：万用表直流档测 VDAC 对 GND（平均值）
用你的读数反算占空比 D = V̄ / 3.3 V
measurements.explain: ≈ 0.25：RC 低通只留下 PWM 的直流分量（平均值），PWM + RC 就是一个 DAC。

measurements.ask: 1 kHz、50 %：示波器测 VDAC 的纹波 Vpp

measurements.explain: τ 只等于一个周期，近似公式不再适用：3.3 × tanh(T/4τ) ≈ 0.81 V，VDAC 在约 1.25 V 和 2.05 V 之间摆——已经不是直流了。
纹波 ∝ 1/f：约 8 mV，是 1 kHz 时的 1/10，平均值不变。提高 PWM 频率能减小纹波，又不会让输出变慢（τ 不变）。

hints: PWM 引脚 → 10 kΩ → VDAC；VDAC 到 GND 接 1 µF；再用跳线把 VDAC 接到一个 ADC1 引脚（GPIO32–39）。
ADC 引脚设成“模拟输入”，另一个引脚设成 PWM。
平均值 = 占空比 × 3.3 V；纹波随频率升高、RC 增大而变小。
